gloss: to lose (someone to death); to be bereaved of

definitions.gloss: to lose (a family member or close person) to death
definitions.explanation: To have someone close die. The subject is the bereaved person, and the object marked by を is the person who died.

examples.japanese: ⟦{去年|きょねん}→去年：00727_kyonen⟧⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{亡|な}くした。
examples.english: I lost my father last year.

examples.japanese: ⟦{幼|おさな}い→幼い：02337_osanai⟧{頃|ころ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{亡|な}くして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: She lost her mother when she was young.

examples.japanese: ⟦{戦争|せんそう}→戦争：01450_sensou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{亡|な}くした⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧たち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}いた→聞く：00483_kiku⟧。
examples.english: I listened to the stories of people who lost family members in the war.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: transitive. The bereaved person is the subject; the person who died is marked with ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧. The intransitive counterpart is ⟦{亡|な}くなる→亡くなる：02639_nakunaru⟧ (to pass away), whose subject is the person who died.
- ⟦{妻|つま}→妻：01005_tsuma⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{亡|な}くす: to lose one's wife
- ⟦{妻|つま}→妻：01005_tsuma⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{亡|な}くなる→亡くなる：02639_nakunaru⟧: one's wife passes away

WRITING:
- {亡|な}くす: to lose a person to death
- ⟦{無|な}くす→無くす：01110_nakusu⟧: to lose an object, to get rid of something
Both are read なくす, so the kanji is what distinguishes them in writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{親|おや}→親：01357_oya⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{亡|な}くす: to lose a parent
- ⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{亡|な}くす: to lose a child
- ⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{亡|な}くす: to lose someone in an accident

ASPECT: {亡|な}くして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ describes the resulting state — the person is bereaved now, not that the loss is in progress.

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {亡|な}くしていませんでした
